subjects.displayTitle: Concealment and disclosure: learning to recognize
subjects.introduction: For years the Manifestation of God moved among people as one of them, and none knew Him. His very appearance, one Tablet declares, was the veil over His face. Concealment here is less a matter of hiding than of seeing: a station can be present, even familiar, and still pass unrecognized by eyes clouded with imaginings. The image unfolds through a garment of camel’s hair, a beauty wrapped in a thousand veils, a word held back because hearts were not yet ready, and at last the appointed hour when the veil is lifted and the call goes out to the world. Strikingly, blame is withheld from those who could not recognize what had not yet been disclosed. Mark tells of Peter naming Jesus as the Christ and being charged to tell no one [1], a kindred mystery of knowing and keeping silent. To ponder this subject is to ask how truth arrives in measure, a question that leads onward to progressive revelation, to wisdom in speech, and to acting according to the needs of each day.
subjects.arc: Begin with the paradox of visible concealment, examine recognition and timing, and distinguish the several meanings of hiddenness.

order.why: Open with manifestation itself becoming a veil.
Locate another veil in the limitations of vision.
Introduce the refusal to blame those who could not yet recognize.
Place hiddenness within years of ordinary presence.
Reinforce the distance between proximity and recognition.
Extend the question to constant companions.
shortened: This was not unique to thee, for even those who were around Him at all times knew Him not, for We veiled the Face behind a thousand veils lest anyone discover what was ordained in the Tablets from the Pen of a holy, protecting One.

order.why: Consider familiar appearance concealing a station.
shortened: Say: Verily the grace, knowledge and wisdom have all appeared in the temple of a concealed Name, Whose manifestation was veiled by His beauty in such wise that none among creation recognized Him, could ye but know it, though He moved among them all the days as one of them, as though they were veiled by their own selves and were as blind, deaf and dumb, in that they beheld not the Beauty of God nor heard the melodies of God, though all these were before their eyes morning and evening.

order.why: Return to presence without recognition.
shortened: Say: This is the Book of Command from the Point of the Bayan unto His servant who hath attained the presence of the Throne yet knew Him not, inasmuch as the Beauty of Glory had veiled His face from the eyes of all the worlds.

order.why: Show the same difficulty in daily company.
Identify imaginings as an obstacle.
Give a particular memory of companionship.
shortened: He is the one who kept company with Me in the land of Ta during the days when the Face was hidden from the worlds.

order.why: Introduce the simple garment as an image.
Let the garment both reveal and veil.
Follow the image toward disclosure.
Read the veil of hair as devotional imagery.
Continue that image in its own source.
Deepen the paradox through the identity of revelation and concealment.
Situate veiling within successive revelation.
shortened: And when this process of progressive Revelation culminated in the stage at which His peerless, His most sacred, and exalted Countenance was to be unveiled to men’s eyes, He chose to hide His own Self behind a thousand veils, lest profane and mortal eyes discover His glory.

And when the set time of concealment was fulfilled, We sent forth, whilst still wrapt within a myriad veils, an infinitesimal glimmer of the effulgent Glory enveloping the Face of the Youth, and lo, the entire company of the dwellers of the Realms above were seized with violent commotion and the favored of God fell down in adoration before Him.

order.why: Ask how a new garment affects recognition.
shortened: O people! It is as though I had never departed from among you, but rather journeyed for days and returned unto you with My Beauty, whose sovereignty every atom doth testify, yet ye knew Me not and denied My Cause, though by it were ye and all contingent beings created. Thereby it hath become evident that in Our former Manifestation ye knew not My Beauty, but only My garment and My robe amidst the earth and heaven. Had ye known My former Beauty, ye would have recognized it in this latter Manifestation when I revealed Myself from behind the veils.

order.why: Read the incomparable concealment of Him Whom God shall make manifest.
Recounts Baha’u’llah’s open support of the Bab despite persecution and danger.
Join recognition to the humility of the Bab.
Introduce the command to remain silent.
Place speech under divine initiative.
Make appointed timing explicit.
shortened: In those days We concealed Our face lest anyone recognize Us, according to the wisdom inscribed in the Tablets by the Pen of Command. When the appointed time of concealment was fulfilled, We unveiled the Face with a sovereignty witnessed by all creation.

order.why: Extend the period before disclosure.
shortened: We remained in this concealment until God's appointed time was fulfilled according to what was ordained by His Pen on a preserved tablet of glory.

order.why: Mark the fulfillment of that time.
Trace months and years toward announcement.
Keep visible presence beside a mission not yet announced.
shortened: However, in those days the appointed time for the Cause had not been fulfilled, therefore We concealed the Face lest the servants recognize it, though it was shining from the horizon of holiness with manifest radiance. When the appointed time was fulfilled, the veils were rent asunder and thy Lord, the Mighty, the Bestower, appeared from behind them and spoke a word whereat all in the heavens and earth were struck with terror.

order.why: Return to a hearer at the moment of disclosure.
shortened: Remember the times when thou wert seated in My presence and didst hear with thine own ears the melodies of God, and in those days We concealed Our face from all who are in the heavens and on earth, according to a wisdom that was hidden in God's mystery. When the appointed time was fulfilled and the Command came forth, We drew aside the veils in Our chosen name and manifested Our Self to all created things with a sovereignty that was witnessed by all worlds.

order.why: Present manifestation as grace.
Follow concealment with renewed appearance.
Preserve the passage’s own symbolic date language.
shortened: When the year nine had passed, He was manifested with this Name [Baha, =9] unto all things, even as thou didst witness how in that year the revelation of the Divine Unity was both hidden yet visible, and manifest yet concealed.

order.why: Bring imprisonment into the narrative of disclosure.
Carry the same transition into courageous testimony.
Consider another account of the veil being lifted.
shortened: Say: We were concealed in a mystery that was, in truth, most beautiful, lest anyone should recognize Us and lest the eyes of the treacherous should fall upon Us. But when the idolaters transgressed beyond their bounds, We removed the veil and revealed the Face with radiant lights of sanctity.

order.why: Confront the reversal of allegiance after disclosure.
Recognize discernment before public announcement.
Consider speech measured to human capacity.
Explore restraint in addressing the people of the Bayan.
Retain the warning about exposing a hidden secret.
shortened: Therefore reveal not a word of what God hath ordained in thy being of the most hidden secret of the testimony of Oneness unto thyself. For if thou shouldst inform them of thy hidden affair, even a little in truth, they would sacrifice themselves for the love of God instead of thee in their longing for God -- and God is truly kind to His servants in truth.

order.why: Read the warning against both exaggeration and hostility.
shortened: Turn people away from exaggeration regarding me, for God knows two groups will perish: the excessive lovers and the hateful detractors. Their sin is not upon me, for I said before and say now before God, His Messengers and His friends that I am a servant who has believed in God and His signs. God has honored me by His grace as He willed with knowledge from the people of infallibility (God's blessings upon them) -- as long as the Sun of Identity has risen with identity and the Sun of Oneness has not set with oneness.

order.why: Hear the claim of servitude in its own terms.
shortened: Say: Verily I am a servant who hath believed in God and His signs, and I say not unto you that I know the unseen, nor do I claim any sign from heaven, but rather I recite unto you these clear verses from the Book of God for a people who remember. Say: Were I to abrogate a decree or command a new decree, then in that moment I would be bound by a true verse from the Book of God. But now verily I am a confirmer of that which ye possess of the pure religion.

order.why: Preserve the stated confirmation of the Furqan.
shortened: And I bear witness before Thee concerning what people attribute to me, that I commanded naught in any book reaching unto all people save the purification of the air, and after making mention of the exaltation of Thy Cause and the Furqan, I joined therewith mention of the confirmation of Thy judgment from before upon all who believed in Thee until Thy judgment should reach them.

order.why: Continue the historical disavowals without erasing their wording.
shortened: Let the copy of the Arabic folio be conveyed by the students to every land, that all may be assured that I am but a servant -- without learning and without claim. Whoso pronounceth concerning this lowly one a judgment of belief to the weight of an atom, God, the All-Knowing, shall question him thereof on the Day of Resurrection. God, and the people of His love, are witnesses and seers that I make no claim that would render obedience to me incumbent upon anyone.

order.why: Allow the explicit retraction to be examined in context.
shortened: This day I beg forgiveness of God, my Lord, for all that I manifested, and I say unto thee -- for the absent ones and for whoso knoweth me -- that I do not stand upon any Cause whose recognition is incumbent upon the people; I lay claim to no authority. And whoso should ascribe to me divine knowledge or authority, upon him be the curse of God, and the curse of His angels, and of all humankind.

order.why: Read the stated conditions of a claim before judging its meaning.
shortened: It is incumbent upon one who claims such a momentous matter that he be characterized by all perfect attributes, both theoretical and practical, and that he lack not any branch of knowledge or custom, and that he have complete and detailed mastery over all outward and inward sciences, and that there be no matter of divine grace or supernatural occurrence that is praiseworthy in God's sight except that he possess it definitively, not merely potentially - like the potential that God has placed in all things, whether essentially or accidentally. And if he lacks any single matter or branch of knowledge, there is no doubt that he is not the bearer of this mighty station. God Almighty and His holy ones bear witness that I am neither learned in, nor capable of, a single branch of the customary sciences, nor the source of any supernatural occurrences.

order.why: Turn to the reported history of another name being promoted.
Keep the related reported words distinguishable in authority.
Distinguish concealment of alleged wrongdoing from concealment of station.
shortened: By God's life! I concealed this with all diligence lest any hateful rejected one should become aware of it. By God! The Pen is powerless to recount what he committed in his vain life, for it is ashamed to mention that which is unworthy of mention this Day.

order.why: Consider withdrawal in response to discord.
shortened: Such hath been ... that the fragrances of discord and dissension from those who profess loyalty have risen to such a degree that the atmosphere of the horizons hath become such that the Ancient Beauty hath determined to veil the effulgence of His peerless Beauty behind the veils of glory, in such wise that no pure light shall ever again be witnessed from Him.

order.why: Read the withdrawal image in another setting.
Distinguish Abdu’l-Baha’s aspiration to servitude.
shortened: You know that I have never desired and do not desire anything except utter evanescence, complete extinction, absolute poverty, and total helplessness.

order.why: Read the wish to conceal within a dialogue of divine love.
Let Joseph’s beauty illuminate the imagery.
shortened: O thou who art enamored of the Joseph of the divine Egypt! The Joseph of Canaan appeared with grace and beauty in the market of earthly Egypt, but the Joseph of the true Beauty appeared in the divine Egypt with a luminous countenance, divine comeliness, heavenly grace, lordly beauty, glorified charm, a brilliant dawning-place, and an appearance like a rose garden in the market of manifestation. And when He found the buyers to be pretenders and the seekers to be heedless, He concealed His luminous countenance behind the veil of the unseen and hid His divine beauty behind the clouds of concealment.

order.why: Follow the image through appearance and departure.
shortened: The Beloved of Reality, Who for ages lay concealed behind the veil of glory and hidden in the mantle of the unseen, hath manifested Himself, and like unto Joseph of Egypt hath appeared in supreme beauty and comeliness, becoming renowned in every street and marketplace.
Blind were they raised, deaf were they gathered, until that Sun of Reality was concealed behind the clouds of glory and vanished in the invisible Kingdom.

order.why: Hear the prayer after absence.
Return to the announcement of the hidden One.
Read the lifting of concealment as a public act.
Make the invitation to the world explicit.
shortened: Today from the rustling of the Divine Lote-Tree this most exalted word is heard: O people of the world! The Hidden Beloved hath appeared and the concealed Mystery hath been made manifest in the assemblage of the world.

order.why: Hear Zion join the proclamation.
Bring the hidden scene into visibility.
shortened: Say: O concourse of humanity! The Most Great Scene hath appeared and hath been adorned with the lights of the countenance of the Lord of Destiny, Who was concealed behind the veils of the Unseen and hidden within His inaccessible knowledge.

order.why: End the linked readings with the appeal of the Beloved.
shortened: O My people! Will ye flee from My presence? Will ye turn away from your Best-Beloved, who loveth you and who standeth now before you? This is the Day wherein the rapture of divine revelation hath taken hold of all created things, the Day wherein He Who had been mentioned in the books of God, the All-Glorious, the All-Wise, hath been made manifest.

order.why: Retain the supplied statement about the measure of disclosure.
Read the supplied mystical warning in its own wording.
Close with the extended provisional disavowal, preserving its translation status.
shortened: Afterward: Thus speaks the least of God's creation, Ali bin Muhammad, the son of the late Muhammad Rida (may his soul rest in peace): A group of people has attributed to this humble servant the claim to the station of Babiyyat (the Gatehood) of the Imam--peace be upon him. However, I have never made such a claim, nor do I make it now.

I myself bear no mastery over any branch of knowledge or practice of the sciences of the learned, nor do I possess the ability to perform any supernatural acts or wonders. If words have flowed from my pen, they have done so purely out of natural inclination, and all of them contradict the norms of the community. These words are evidence of nothing.

questions: How do these passages distinguish being physically present from being recognized?
What different meanings of concealment emerge when timing, human capacity, protection, and devotion are considered separately?
How does the passage that withholds blame complicate a quick judgment about failure to recognize?
What does Mark’s account of Peter’s recognition and the ensuing silence add to the question of disclosure?
How might the historical disavowals and expressions of servitude be studied without forcing them into a single explanation?
What guidance about wise communication emerges beside the connected subjects of progressive revelation and the needs of the time?

references.label: 1 · Mark 8:27–30 · Recognition and an instruction to silence
references.note: In the King James Version, Jesus asks the disciples who they believe he is. Peter identifies him as the Christ, and Jesus then charges them to tell no one. Compare the distinction between recognition and public disclosure with the compilation’s accounts of concealment. The passage opens a question about communication without establishing that every historical instance has the same purpose.

subjects.displayTitle: Earlier scriptures: reading with recognition and respect
subjects.introduction: To love the light, ‘Abdu’l-Bahá says, is to welcome it from whatever lamp it shines, Israelite or Arab, Persian or Indian. That single affection changes how a person opens the Torah, the Gospel, the Qur’an or the counsels of Zoroaster and Buddha: not as rivals to be ranked, but as heralds sent from one Will to teach love, justice and peace, and to lift whole peoples from ignorance to understanding. Bahá’u’lláh asks his followers to know these books, to see how the religion of Jesus became the religion of Muhammad and lives on in the faith they now profess, and to recognize in every confirming revelation the same seed bearing new fruit. The Qur’an’s own word that it confirms earlier scripture while allowing different ways and testing each people by what it has been given [1] opens a fruitful comparison. Reading this way soon raises other questions: how progressive revelation holds its many messengers together, which parts of religion endure and which must change, and why a tradition that begins in light can need renewal. The invitation is as practical as it is wide: study the books, observe what their teachings cultivate in a life, and let recognition of a shared purpose deepen friendship without erasing honest difference.
subjects.arc: Begin with love of the light and the duty to study, then consider continuity, renewal, particular traditions, and the conduct recognition requires.

order.why: Follow successive religions through their due functions.
Open with love of light across different sources.
Turn recognition into the obligation to study.
Name the virtues toward which the books guide.
shortened: The Heavenly Books, the Bible, the Qur'an, and the other Holy Writings have been given by God as guides into the paths of Divine virtue, love, justice and peace.

order.why: Connect shared teaching to the order of the world.
Offer the image of scriptures as lamps and cords.
Present each book as a herald of guidance.
Consider the enduring testimony of written revelation.
Honor the Torah and Gospel explicitly.
Include the range of books named by the Bab.
Read the recognition of Moses and Christ within Islam.
shortened: The people of Islam were taught to realize how Jesus came from God and was born of the Spirit, and that He must be glorified of all men. Moses was a prophet of God, and revealed in His day and for the people to whom He was sent, the Book of God.
Muhammad recognized the sublime grandeur of Christ and the greatness of Moses and the prophets.

order.why: Continue that recognition in the Qur’an.
Hear a later book confirm its predecessors.
Identify the educational work of the Prophets.
shortened: The divine Prophets have revealed and founded religion. They have laid down certain laws and heavenly principles for the guidance of mankind. They have taught and promulgated the knowledge of God, established praiseworthy ethical ideals and inculcated the highest standards of virtues in the human world.

order.why: Emphasize mercy as their purpose.
shortened: It has been shown incontrovertibly that God chose the Prophets as a mercy in all worlds, and not as a chastisement on the wayfarers. They all summoned the people to the path of guidance and held fast to the sure handle, and thus they delivered degenerate peoples from the nadir of ignorance and blindness and led them to the apex of excellence and understanding.

order.why: Place succession within progressive revelation.
Examine the developmental analogy in its theological setting.
Introduce Abraham’s continuing legacy.
shortened: This exile resulted in the appearance of the Prophets of Israel from the progeny of Abraham--and so will it continue forevermore.

order.why: Retain the compilation’s account of prophetic lineage.
shortened: Thus the descendants of Abraham received the special blessing that all the Prophets of the House of Israel were raised up from among their ranks. This is a blessing that God bestowed upon that lineage. Moses, through both His father and His mother; Christ, through His mother; Muhammad; the Bab; and all the Prophets and Holy Ones of Israel belong to that lineage. Baha'u'llah too is a lineal descendant of Abraham, for Abraham had other sons besides Ishmael and Isaac who in those days emigrated to the regions of Persia and Afghanistan, and the Blessed Beauty is one of their descendants.

order.why: Widen the stated unity to Zoroaster and Buddha.
shortened: For example, His Holiness Zoroaster was a prophet, precisely according to the Messianic example. There was no difference whatsoever between the spirit of the teachings which Zoroaster gave and those which His Holiness the Christ gave. Likewise the teachings of Buddha are not at all opposed to the teachings of the Christ, or to the teachings of any of the prophets. These great and blessed souls had for their aim the same principle. Their purpose was one, their law was one, their teaching was one.

order.why: Question recognition limited to named Qur’anic figures.
Consider Zoroaster through the conduct his teachings foster.
shortened: In numerous passages in the divine Tablets, blessed mention is made of Zoroaster with utmost praise, for that blessed being was one of the Manifestations of the Divine Unity and became the cause of guidance for a great nation. Whoever studies the teachings and counsels of that noble one will clearly see that those teachings are heavenly and those counsels are the words of a divine person. And as long as the Parsees acted according to the counsels and admonitions of that noble one, they were cherished in both worlds, but when they became deprived of that conduct and behavior, that eternal glory was transformed.

order.why: Hear the comparison of Buddha and Christ.
Keep the assessment of later Buddhist teachings in its attributed context.
Read the discussion of other traditions and available writings.
shortened: As for other religions, in the texts of Baha'u'llah and writings of the friends, such as the book of Mirza Abu'l-Fadl, there are explicit mentions of Zoroaster, Buddha, Brahma and Confucius. Similarly in my letters, the original foundations of Zoroaster and Buddha were very compatible but were later altered and changed.

order.why: Retain the account of the religion of Jamshid.
Return to the theme of human unity.
Consider the continuing power to shape lives.
Read the seed and its enduring fruit.
shortened: Observe how Christ and Muhammad sowed a seed that until now yields fruit, while all other farmers ultimately failed and lost.

order.why: Distinguish confirmation and renewal from simple cancellation.
Consider new life given to ancient meanings.
Hear the appeal to fulfillment.
Separate enduring sovereignty from changing organization.
Explore the image of recovered gold.
Consider compassion and justice as continuing concerns.
Read the reported image of an ancient path cleared anew.
Bring misunderstanding and imitation into the discussion.
Retain the old-tree analogy as an attributed assessment.
Consider the reported limits of historical reach.
shortened: Because of this the teachings of Moses were confined to Palestine. The cause of Jesus Christ was spread over some parts of Europe, Asia and Africa, and the cause of Mohammed over some parts of Europe, Asia and Africa; none were universal.

order.why: Preserve this reported historical claim without adopting it as a general account.
shortened: At the time of Mohammed, no one believed in Christ, so Christ was first preached by Mohammed. Then they were given the teachings of Mohammed.

order.why: Read the polemical comparison of the size and composition of scriptures.
shortened: For example, the followers of the Gospel hold fast to a few pages, and by these limited pages consider themselves superior to and better than all other peoples. And before that, the Torah, which was specific to Moses, consisted of a few books. They have gathered various sayings of the Prophets like Isaiah, Ezekiel, Solomon, David, Jeremiah, Zechariah and others into one volume, though most parts of it are historical accounts written after Moses. Then came the decree of the Furqan (Qur'an), which in truth distinguishes between right and wrong.
And now, many equivalents to all these have been revealed and are available and evident.

order.why: Examine the stated authority of Holy Writ.
Turn to signs and nested meanings in sacred books.
Consider a mystery understood through a later appearance.
shortened: Thus, the reality of Christ's appearance in the Mosaic Dispensation was one of the divine mysteries that later became revealed and manifest through the appearance of Christ.

order.why: Introduce the claim of foretold light.
Read fulfillment through the image of promised water.
shortened: This is what they who have near access to God have attained. This is the flowing water ye were promised in the Qur'an, and later in the Bayan, as a recompense from your Lord, the God of Mercy. Blessed are they that quaff it.

order.why: Hear continuity expressed through several prophetic names.
Consider the Most Great Book and its scriptural preamble.
shortened: The Books have been sealed by the Most Great Book wherein is detailed the knowledge of what hath been and what shall be.
The preamble of this Book hath been adorned with that which was foretold in the Psalms, the Qur'an, the Gospel and what was revealed in the Holy Books.

order.why: Relates the evidence for this Revelation to that for earlier Scriptures.
Let personified scriptures join the proclamation.
Read the reception of biblical glad tidings.
shortened: O thou who hast confessed and believed in the Words of God!

Thank God, for He hath uncovered the veil from before thine eye, and that thou hast witnessed the great signs of the greatest glad-tidings which have been revealed in the Gospel, Bible and the Psalms; and wert confirmed that verily those glad-tidings have allusions to the appearance of the Kingdom of God during this time, and that the horizons shall brighten through the light of the effulgence in this age, which is the age of the lights and the century of thy God, the Powerful, the Almighty!

order.why: Retain the reported expectation of fulfilled promise.
shortened: This golden thread of promise concerning the Messianic Millennium is running through the Bible and it was so destined that God in its own good time will cause its appearance. Not even a single word will be left meaningless or unfulfilled.

order.why: Ask why praise of a past revelation can coexist with resistance to a new one.
Read the Bab’s demanding account of continued fidelity.
shortened: There is no way for you to believe in the Qur'an except that ye believe in the Bayan, and it is the same whether ye believe or believe not. Would any among you be content to say at this time "I follow the religion of Jesus"? If not, then how can ye be content to follow that which ye now follow? That which Jesus - peace be upon Him - revealed of religion was from God; this became the religion of Muhammad in His Manifestation, and this became the religion of your Qa'im in His Manifestation.

order.why: Consider the reported analogy of successive governors.
Return to following light from different dawning points.
Move recognition into a public interreligious encounter.
Retain the appeal to justice in such an encounter.
Follow the work of explaining prophetic validity.
shortened: In most of these places I spoke to them about the original foundations of the divine religions and I explained to them the proofs of the validity of the divine prophets and of the holy Manifestations.

order.why: Notice believers defending a tradition other than their inherited one.
End the linked testimony with fidelity to Christ.
shortened: Consider with what knowledge His holiness Baha'u'llah hath favored the Baha'is, that if they are given the whole world they will not deny Christ.

order.why: Open a further comparison through new birth.
shortened: The sacred books of all nations speak of the possibility of the new birth of man. What does this mean?
A child in the matrix of its mother is in utter darkness. When it is born into the world it comes into the light.

order.why: Hold the enduring traces of truth in view.
shortened: The traces of truth cannot be eliminated. Even if all who dwell on earth were to unite and wish to obliterate the divine traces, they would be powerless to do so.

order.why: Read the supplied Qur’anic affirmation of the Prophets.
Preserve the supplied statement of progressive revelation.
Close with the supplied image of messengers sent among nations.

questions: What would it mean to honor a scripture through the way you read it and treat its followers?
How do these passages relate continuing spiritual principles to changing religious laws and circumstances?
What questions arise when the compilation’s assessments of a tradition are compared with that tradition’s own account of itself?
How does Qur’an 5:48 connect confirmation of scripture, difference, and the practice of good deeds?
Why might loyalty to an earlier teacher sometimes make recognition of a later one difficult?
Which connected subject would help you investigate the relationship between renewal, religious unity, and genuine differences?

references.label: 1 · Qur’an 5:48 · Confirmation, different paths, and good deeds
references.note: Mustafa Khattab’s translation presents the Qur’an as confirming earlier scripture and exercising authority in relation to it. The verse also speaks of differing laws and ways, testing through what has been given, and striving in good deeds. Compare these themes with the Bahá’í account of continuity and renewal, allowing Islamic and Bahá’í understandings of revelation to remain distinct.

subjects.displayTitle: Caring for vulnerable people: dignity made practical
subjects.introduction: Bahá’u’lláh tells the wealthy that when they meet someone poor and dust-stained they are not to hurry past but to sit down and ask what has happened to them, and that in such a moment the inhabitants of heaven pray for them. Care for the vulnerable begins there, in a relationship that treats the other as an equal rather than a case. The poor are a trust of God to be answered for; the orphan is to find a loving father, the sick a nurse, the stranger a refuge, and ‘Abdu’l-Bahá asks that no one rest until each person in their care feels like a member of the family. Food comes before religious talk, schooling and livelihoods follow relief, and the House of Justice is made a shelter for those whose families cannot provide. James presses the same point when he contrasts the welcome given to a rich visitor with the humiliation of a poor one and dismisses goodwill that leaves a hungry person unfed [1]. The question is not only who stands in need today but what allows need to persist, and it leads to service as a way of life, to the moderation of inequality, and even to the kindness owed to animals.
subjects.arc: Begin with dignity and listening, move through practical care and education, and widen personal generosity into organized responsibility.

order.why: Hear the poor described as a divine trust.
Open with sitting beside a person in poverty and listening.
shortened: O ye that are rich! When ye behold one who is poor and dust-stained, flee not from him, but rather sit with him and ask concerning that which hath befallen him from the seas of God's decree. By God, in that state the denizens of the Supreme Concourse will observe you, and will pray for you, and will implore forgiveness for you, and will extol and glorify you with sanctified, pure and eloquent tongues.

order.why: Make equal honor across peoples explicit.
shortened: O daughter of the kingdom show the greatest respect and honour to the poor, to the orphans and the disabled from every land, from every tribe and people. Show the utmost loving kindness to them and serve them as a true servant might. Treat them as thou wouldst the most honourable and dignified people in the land and place thyself at their disposal both by night and day.

order.why: Ground material sharing in common creation.
shortened: O concourse of princes! Turn ye unto the poor. God hath created you and them from one thing. Make ye in your possessions a portion for them. This will profit you throughout ages and centuries.

order.why: Add accountability to that trust.
shortened: Know ye that the poor are the trust of God in your midst. Watch that ye betray not His trust, that ye deal not unjustly with them and that ye walk not in the ways of the treacherous. Ye will most certainly be called upon to answer for His trust on the day when the Balance of Justice shall be set, the day when unto everyone shall be rendered his due, when the doings of all men, be they rich or poor, shall be weighed.

order.why: Picture divine attention to each grief-stricken person.
shortened: Verily, I commune with every poor one, sit with every lowly one, turn toward every oppressed one, and behold every grief-stricken one.

order.why: Question the equation of poverty with low worth.
Bring the person within the circle of family.
Name the many forms compassionate service can take.
shortened: Be ye loving fathers to the orphan, and a refuge to the helpless, and a treasury for the poor, and a cure for the ailing. Be ye the helpers of every victim of oppression, the patrons of the disadvantaged.

order.why: Join respect with nursing and assistance.
Extend refuge to strangers and people who are ill.
shortened: In treating the poor, the weak, the needy and the strangers, provide blessed healing and guide them to health and wellbeing.
Give great importance to the matter of the poor - be a refuge and shelter to every poor one, and a protector and helper to every sick one.

order.why: Turn the aspiration into sustained daily effort.
Imagine a community becoming shelter and assistance.
shortened: May they become a treasure of wealth for every poor one, a refuge and shelter for every seeker of protection, a spirit and delight for the destitute, and divine assistance for the helpless.

order.why: Place food before religious talk in this reported counsel.
Name food, clothing, and care for orphans.
Read concrete acts of generosity in a remembered life.
shortened: For fifty years the Blessed Beauty showed kindness to these people - if they saw a barefoot person from the window, He would order shoes bought for them; if they saw someone naked, He would give them clothes; if they saw someone poor, He would give them charity; if they saw someone weak, He would give them food.

order.why: Retain the reported provision of food at the speaker’s expense.
Consider help during reversals of livelihood.
shortened: The inhabitants of these parts know this and therefore whenever they are in difficulties or have had business reverses they come to us and we will never send them away unaided or deprived.

order.why: Read mutual assistance in a particular period of difficulty.
shortened: Therefore their worldly affairs and livelihood have fallen into extreme difficulty, and in such cases the friends must certainly assist one another.

order.why: Attend to the surviving families of martyrs.
shortened: The purpose is that all should strive with all their powers to ensure that each of the martyrs' survivors lives in the utmost comfort and happiness.

order.why: Explore the comfort of visiting a sick person.
shortened: We should all visit the sick. When they are in sorrow and suffering, it is a real help and benefit to have a friend come. Happiness is a great healer to those who are ill.
This has greater effect than the remedy itself. You must always have this thought of love and affection when you visit the ailing and afflicted.

order.why: Read nursing and visiting across religious boundaries.
Consider the manner of speech during a visit.
shortened: When visiting the sick, speak of spiritual qualities and divine conduct and behavior without mentioning names or being explicit. Better that the secrets of the beloved ones be told in stories of others.

order.why: Join material assistance to spiritual companionship.
shortened: Be nurses to the sick, treasurers for the poor, and supply heavenly food to the hungry.

order.why: Retain the remembered visit to children in poverty.
Ask how hospitality can bring gladness.
Read the call to love the poor in its reported terms.
Keep direct companionship in view.
Link companionship with forbearance under suffering.
shortened: Let us, in all fidelity offer our breasts as targets for the arrows of cruelty and at the same time possess a sin-covering eye; let us associate with the poor and be the companions of the needy.

order.why: Give the education of orphans a central place.
shortened: In this holy Cause the question of orphans hath the utmost importance. The greatest consideration must be shown towards orphans; they must be taught, trained and educated.

order.why: Move from family responsibility to institutional provision.
shortened: Unto every father hath been enjoined the instruction of his son and daughter in the art of reading and writing and in all that hath been laid down in the Holy Tablet. He that putteth away that which is commanded unto him, the Trustees are then to take from him that which is required for their instruction if he be wealthy and, if not, the matter devolveth upon the House of Justice. Verily have We made it a shelter for the poor and needy.

order.why: Honor education as service.
Consider the teacher’s work with destitute children.
shortened: Today, at the Threshold of His Holiness Baha'u'llah, there is nobody more favored than thee, because thou art busy in the service of the orphans and in the education of the destitute, helpless children.

order.why: Read the reported contrast about gratitude without making it a condition of support.
shortened: Therefore, distinction, honor and benevolence toward humanity lie in educating orphaned children and the children of the poor and weak, for such children will always remain grateful and appreciative of their benefactors, and will be more content and thankful, unlike children who consider themselves entitled heirs and see their parents as obligated to educate them - they are not as appreciative nor as eager to learn and grateful to their teachers as other children without guardians become.

order.why: Challenge assumptions about the future of orphaned children.
Join schooling and care to industry and livelihoods.
shortened: The fourth obligation is the protection and preservation of all the friends in all circumstances and situations, and the administration of general affairs such as the education of children, refinement of character, teaching of beneficial sciences in all aspects, establishment of schools for both males and females, caring for the poor and weak and young and orphans and widows, and devising means of industry and livelihood and improvement of general conditions.

order.why: Consider a society organized for these purposes.
shortened: Rather, the loved ones of God must strive with heart and soul so that day by day this society may gain strength and engage in service to the Cause - educating children, nurturing orphans, helping the poor, spreading knowledge, and becoming a means of guiding people.

order.why: Make consultation about care explicit.
shortened: "Their fourth duty is to meditate and consult for the helping of the poor and the weak and the protection of the sick.

order.why: Move beyond immediate aid toward preventing greater poverty.
Identifies practical assistance to those in need as evidence of faith.
Put access to influential people at the service of those in need.
shortened: The alms-tax of associating with people of influence and authority is helping the poor in conducting their affairs or identifying resources."

order.why: Consider willing generosity as an expression of virtue.
Explore the freedom and joy of sharing surplus.
Place generosity within care for self, family, and others.
shortened:
The essence of charity is for the servant to recount the
blessings of his Lord, and to render thanks unto Him at all
times and under all conditions.

The beginning of magnanimity is when man expendeth
his wealth on himself, on his family and on the poor among
his brethren in his Faith.

order.why: Recognize charity among good deeds.
Stress the continuing necessity of assistance.
shortened: To care for the weak is essential and to assist the poor is among those things most necessary before the All-Forgiving, and shall ever be so. I swear by the Sun of sanctified glory that has risen from the horizon of the prison, that the cry of those who are oppressed among the loved ones of God and the poor among His friends has been and shall ever be effective.

order.why: Connect practical kindness to truthfulness and discernment.
shortened: The Lord of the worlds declareth: O servants! Abandon your desires and seek that which I have desired for you. Travel not the way without a guide, nor accept every guide's words. Many guides are themselves astray and have not found the right path. A guide is one who is free from the bonds of the world and whom nothing preventeth from speaking the truth.
O servants! Practice truthfulness, turn not away from the destitute, make mention of Me before the great ones, and fear not.

order.why: Read care for the poor as part of the teachings.
shortened: Deliver my message to Mrs. Lehman and tell her that service to the friends is service to the Kingdom of God and care for the poor is among the divine teachings.

order.why: Encourage the desire to make lives fruitful.
shortened: Those souls who are of the Kingdom eagerly wish to be of service to the poor, to sympathize with them, to show kindness to the miserable and to make their lives fruitful. Happy art thou that thou hast such a wish.

order.why: Recognize the difference between intention and available means.
shortened: For instance, a man may have the intention to succor the poor and assist the orphan, but be without the necessary means with which to carry it out.

order.why: Notice an accepted offering followed by assistance of greater value.
shortened: And yet, when an offering was adorned with the glory of His acceptance and reported by Jinab-i-Amin, twice that amount was ordered to be paid out to the poor and the needy.

order.why: Read a particular gift redirected toward need.
shortened: You had written that you have presented a spice shop as a gift to 'Abdu'l-Baha. This gift is accepted, but you should sell it and spend its proceeds on the poor among the friends.

order.why: Retain the personal account of sacrifice for winter clothing.
Consider the fruitful seed as an image of generosity.
shortened: Those distinguished souls who in the past year assisted the poor - I beseech from God's favors that their charity may become like a seed that produces seven ears, in each ear a hundred grains, and God multiplies for whom He wishes.

order.why: Read the invocation of giving in the Qur’an.
shortened: O sincere friends of the Greatest Name! In the Qur'an, spending of one's substance is specified as a characteristic of the people of faith, and it is revealed "they strive with their wealth and their lives."

order.why: Carry mindfulness of poverty across generations.
Honor sustained care for helpless people and orphans.
Recognize the happiness of serving.
Return to service as a way of worship.
Close the linked readings with comforting the downtrodden.
Bring the supplied statement of material and spiritual social service into view.

questions: What changes when assistance begins with listening and equal respect?
How might immediate relief, education, livelihood, and prevention of poverty support one another?
What can a community learn from those who receive help when it plans its service?
How does James’s treatment of favoritism challenge the ways people are welcomed in religious gatherings?
What forms of companionship during illness can express love while respecting the person’s needs and choices?
How do the connected subjects of inequality, service, and kindness to animals broaden the responsibilities explored here?

references.label: 1 · James 2:1–17 · Equal welcome and practical help
references.note: The King James Version contrasts the welcome given to a wealthy visitor with the humiliation of a poor one, then questions goodwill that leaves a hungry or unclothed person unaided. Read the passage alongside the compilation’s emphasis on dignity, listening, and material assistance. Consider how a community’s ordinary arrangements reveal what it believes about the worth of people.

subjects.displayTitle: The dignity of learning: knowledge that benefits the world
subjects.introduction: Knowledge, Bahá’u’lláh says, is wings to a human life and a ladder for its ascent, a treasure and a source of joy, and the claim of scientists and craftsmen on the peoples of the world is great indeed. ‘Abdu’l-Bahá goes further and calls knowledge love: the mirror in which all things are reflected, the inheritance by which one person receives what all humanity has discovered. There is a condition, though. The sciences worth acquiring are those that profit the peoples of the earth, not those that begin and end in words, and the learned must be lit candles, joining intellectual power to good character, humility and the fear of God, or their height and girth are no better than dead wood. Confucius, who warned against study without thought and defined knowledge as knowing what one does and does not know, keeps good company with these counsels [1]. The astronomer who danced on his roof at finding a planet’s true place shows the pleasure that waits in understanding; the teacher of children and the student urged to excel show its duties. The road from here leads to the call to acquire knowledge itself, to the sciences and arts that build civilization, to the education of children, and to the grim history of books destroyed by those who feared them.
subjects.arc: Begin with the joy and public value of knowledge, examine character and intellectual humility, and follow learning into teaching and social progress.

order.why: Open with knowledge as wings, treasure, and public benefit.
shortened: Knowledge is as wings to man's life, and a ladder for his ascent. Its acquisition is incumbent upon everyone. The knowledge of such sciences, however, should be acquired as can profit the peoples of the earth, and not those which begin with words and end with words.  Great indeed is the claim of scientists and craftsmen on the peoples of the world.

In truth, knowledge is a veritable treasure for man, and a source of glory, of bounty, of joy, of exaltation, of cheer and gladness unto him. Happy the man that cleaveth unto it, and woe betide the heedless.

order.why: Introduce the startling association of knowledge and love.
Present learning as access to humanity’s accumulated discoveries.
Join past and present through scientific inquiry.
Survey the many powers of knowledge.
Make the use of the mind a central responsibility.
shortened: There are certain pillars which have been established as the unshakeable supports of the Faith of God. The mightiest of these is learning and the use of the mind, the expansion of consciousness, and insight into the realities of the universe and the hidden mysteries of Almighty God.
To promote knowledge is thus an inescapable duty imposed on every one of the friends of God.

order.why: Set careful investigation against thoughtless imitation.
Widen useful learning to the mysteries of creation.
Ask whether knowledge serves salvation or destruction.
Focus the criterion of benefit to humanity.
shortened: In the Most Holy Book We have commanded all people to acquire sciences, crafts and such other things as will benefit mankind. By sciences is meant beneficial sciences, not those which begin and end in mere words.

order.why: Return to the claim of scientists and craftspeople.
Read the forceful fruitful-tree image as an appeal to develop capacities.
shortened: A person without knowledge and crafts is not beloved - like trees without fruit have they been and ever shall be.

order.why: Join knowledge, craft, and conduct as human adornment.
shortened: O people of Baha! Man's adornment consisteth not in the things of this world, but rather in the knowledge of God - exalted be His glory - and in sciences, crafts and proper conduct.

order.why: Examine the character required of the learned.
shortened: The spiritually learned must be characterized by both inward and outward perfections; they must possess a good character, an enlightened nature, a pure intent, as well as intellectual power, brilliance and discernment, intuition, discretion and foresight, temperance, reverence, and a heartfelt fear of God. For an unlit candle, however great in diameter and tall, is no better than a barren palm tree or a pile of dead wood.

order.why: Bring sciences and good intentions together.
shortened: If outward sciences are combined with good intentions and praiseworthy character, they become light upon light, illumining the world of the soul, making human life and form a mirror of the divine image and likeness, reflecting the realms above.

order.why: Confront the danger of intellectual pride.
shortened: Although to acquire the sciences and arts is the greatest glory of mankind, this is so only on condition that manis river flow into the mighty sea, and draw from Godis ancient source His inspiration. When this cometh to pass, then every teacher is as a shoreless ocean, every pupil a prodigal fountain of knowledge. If, then, the pursuit of knowledge lead to the beauty of Him Who is the Object of all Knowledge, how excellent that goal; but if not, a mere drop will perhaps shut a man off from flooding grace, for with learning cometh arrogance and pride, and it bringeth on error and indifference to God.

order.why: Question any automatic equation of credentials and recognition.
shortened: How many shepherds in the days of the Dawning-Places of Revelation and the Daysprings of Inspiration attained to the knowledge and recognition of God, exalted be His glory, while how many divines and doctors remained deprived.

order.why: Allow differing responses among the learned.
shortened: How many a learned one turned away from the Cause, and how many a learned one spent what he possessed in My path and bore hardships in My love, the Mighty, the Inaccessible.

order.why: Consider branches in relation to spiritual roots.
Read the theological account of intellect in its own terms.
Retain the reported comparison of human and animal intelligence.
shortened: The power of the intellect is one of God's greatest gifts to men, it is the power that makes him a higher creature than the animal. For whereas, century by century and age by age man's intelligence grows and becomes keener, that of the animal remains the same.

order.why: Bring judgment, evidence, and historical writing into view.
shortened: Man should weigh all questions with the power of the intellect.
History, which is a great science, should be written by academies, not by individuals, liable to be influenced by emotions.

order.why: Picture wisdom as a guide and protector.
Contrast the endurance of learning with political dominion.
Develop the image of sovereignty in understanding.
shortened: O king of the country of knowledge!

The world-conquering kings strive for years with utmost vigor and devotion crying out and making sacrifices to conquer this country of dust, and rule this dark heap and at the end repose underneath it.
Through the mercy of God ye became the king of the country of knowledge and the sovereign of the world of understanding.

order.why: Connect learning to the fortunes of nations.
Consider a school as an instrument of renewal.
shortened: This school is of utmost importance. In all existence there is nothing greater than wisdom. It is knowledge and learning that cause the advancement of nations. It is knowledge and learning that guide humanity and bring illumination. It is knowledge and learning that bring prosperity and development. It is knowledge and learning that transform a wasteland into a rose garden. It is knowledge and learning that make a wilderness into a paradise. It is knowledge and learning that exalt abased nations. Therefore, in all existence, the most important of matters is knowledge and learning.

order.why: Read the hope for a particular school’s progress.
shortened: If proper effort is exerted as it should be, that school will undoubtedly, through divine assistance and favor, progress to such a degree that it will surpass all other schools, and in the future will reach such a level that it becomes the foremost school in the world.

order.why: Observe the breadth and diligence of a learned life.
shortened: Early in life, this illustrious man attended institutions of higher learning and labored diligently, by day and night, until he became thoroughly conversant with the learning of the day, with secular studies, philosophy, and religious jurisprudence.

He reflected day and night on the most abstruse of spiritual questions, and gazed in wonderment at the mighty signs of God as written in the Book of Life. He became thoroughly versed even in such material sciences as mathematics, geometry, and geography; in brief, he was well grounded in many fields, thoroughly conversant with the thought of ancient and modern times.

order.why: Connect broad knowledge with human oneness.
shortened: How erudite and learned he was! He had marvel knowledge of the contents of books. He was well informed  the tenets of every religion and had mastered the intricate laws and complicated customs of every nation - ancient and modern. He knew in detail the doctrines of every sect or party, and was a standard-bearer of the oneness of the world of humanity.

order.why: Read another tribute to learning across traditions.
shortened: How learned was he! How wise was he! How well-informed was he! His understanding was marvelous and his wisdom beyond comparison. He was acquainted with the master-thoughts of the authors of every nation, he was equipped with the Knowledge of the Holy Scriptures of all the religions. He knew the contents of Zand Avesta and the Zoroastrian literature. He had a most comprehensive knowledge of the Bible and the Gospel. He was apprised of their inner meanings. He had mastered the opinions and theories of the philosophers of the past, and the Ideals of the spiritual scholars were known to him.

order.why: Include eloquence and spiritual influence in that portrait.
shortened: He was a learned and wise man. He had studied deeply the different branches of Knowledge. He was a theologian, a philosopher, a Sufi and a Baha'i. The eloquence and fluency of his tongue was matchless and when he began to speak he moved the hearts of men with the power of the Spirit.

order.why: Retain the historical account of Farabi’s many capacities.
shortened: According to oriental history there have come in the past two Teachers in philosophy. The first one is Aristotle who was well-versed in all the sciences and accomplishments of his time. The second teacher was Farabi who announced that he is the second teacher. The King ordered the organization of an Academy of learned men and Farabi was examined by the master of every branch of Knowledge. Not only he demonstrated that he knows as much as they know, but he established his superiority over them. Even he was examined in musical art of his time and displayed his marvellous versatility and many sidedness.

order.why: Let the pleasures of discovery and useful work become vivid.
shortened: An engineer spans a large river with a suspension or cantilever bridge, or an architect makes the design of an edifice. Each finds true enjoyment in his work.

It is related that Baseer Tousy was well versed in the science of astronomy. Many nights he walked on the roof of his house watching the stars. Whenever he happened to discover the true position of a planet or to locate the place of a constellation he became so enraptured with the joy of a new idea that he would get up and dance and sing, saying: 'Where are the kings?

order.why: Examine the reported challenge to learning without practical fruit.
Honor study of the divine books.
Read the prayer for evidence and understanding.
Encourage scholarly discussion and reasoned exposition.
shortened: Regarding your intention to compose a treatise proving the Cause of God - the divine friends must devote their thoughts and mention day and night to divine proofs and evidences, engage in scholarly discussions, and employ rational and traditional arguments, so that each one may be able to compose treatises and become the manifestation of "We have given him knowledge from Our presence."

order.why: Picture scholarship in service to others.
shortened: Blessed is the scholar who arose to serve My Cause, made known unto men My path and guided them to the ocean of My mercy and the heaven of My loving-kindness.

order.why: Read the station of scholars who turn toward recognition.
shortened: This exalted rank and most high station has been and continues to be reserved for the learned ones - those scholars who have turned to the supreme horizon and attained the highest summit, which is the station of recognition of God, exalted be His glory. They are as lights for the darkness of the earth and as stars for the heavens of understanding.

order.why: Honor the teacher of children.
Link teaching to faithful responsibility.
Consider education through the image of nurturing growth.
shortened: Among the greatest of all services that can possibly be rendered by man to Almighty God is the education and training of children, young plants of the Abha Paradise, so that these children, fostered by grace in the way of salvation, growing like pearls of divine bounty in the shell of education, will one day bejewel the crown of abiding glory.

order.why: Encourage the learner as a flourishing tree.
shortened: It is my hope that thou wilt become a child of the Kingdom, wilt study arts, sciences and divine knowledge, mayest turn into a fruitful and flourishing tree in the Vineyard of God and that, through the sprinkling of the clouds of His loving providence, thou mayest appear in the utmost freshness and tender beauty.

order.why: Join effort in sciences and arts to the divine image.
shortened: And among the greatest of these attributes of perfection are wisdom and knowledge. Ye must therefore put forth a mighty effort, striving by night and day and resting not for a moment, to acquire an abundant share of all the sciences and arts, that the Divine Image, which shineth out from the Sun of Truth, may illumine the mirror of the hearts of men.

order.why: Places the acquisition of sciences and arts among humanity’s greatest excellences.
Read the hope that students will enlighten their country.
Connect strenuous study to the advancement of Iran.
Retain the appeal to excel in knowledge.
shortened: In science and acquisition of knowledge, the friends of God must excel over all people and rank first. If they study medicine, they must become teachers, so that others are taught the same science. They must endeavor to pass this learning to many others, because becoming a physician is not sufficient.

order.why: Name practical trades and professions among worthy studies.
shortened: Learn the arts, study the sciences, acquire the practical methods of knowledges, trades and professions, learn the most useful crafts of the age;- thus you may be honored amongst men and respected by all the people.

order.why: Bring attention to lessons and writing.
shortened: You should think much of your lessons and your writing, which will fit you to be useful men.

order.why: Read disciplined study within a particular counsel to a young believer.
shortened: A wise young man ever thinks of and studies those means which are conducive to his progress - mental, intellectual and spiritual. He lets all amusements and recreations go and applies himself to the acquirement of knowledge - thus he may become a useful member of the body politic.

order.why: Return to the continuing command to acquire sciences and arts.
shortened: Regarding what was mentioned about engagement in sciences and arts, after it was presented in His presence, He said: "This matter has been mentioned in most of the Tablets and all are commanded to it. The adornment of man is through perfection.

order.why: Picture knowledge and wisdom as ornaments.
Honor educational leadership as service to humanity.
Connect university education with universal peace.
Read the weapons of knowledge as resistance to ignorance.
shortened: Tell me of our battle, in which we resist with the hosts of divine confirmation and victory against the armies of darkness of the natural world, and with the weapons of knowledge and wisdom we defeat the army of ignorance and delusion.

order.why: Consider a human life as a book of experience.
shortened: The days of man and the life of the wise ones consist of an inscribed book, an unfolded scroll, and a preserved tablet wherein in all its pages and tablets events are written, and in all its leaves and wonders realities of occurrences and mysteries are inscribed.

order.why: Close the linked readings with a prayer that study becomes service.
shortened: O Lord! Open before their faces the gates of knowledge, fill their hearts with the realities of the arts and sciences, and make the endings of their studies the beginnings of success and prosperity, that they may attain to every joy and gladness and increase day by day in faith and certitude, in serenity and assurance, that they may serve Thy servants in Thy land and worship at Thy holy Threshold.

order.why: Read the explicit supplied clarification that philosophy is a sound field of learning.
Join research principles to love and growing understanding.
Face the challenge of relating specialized disciplines.
Connect deep understanding with the questions of the wider world.
Close with the contribution experts can make to society.

questions: Which image of learning best expresses what has drawn you to study?
How might the benefit of a field of knowledge extend beyond its most immediate practical uses?
What habits can join intellectual rigor with humility and good character?
How do Confucius’s counsels about reflection and acknowledging uncertainty speak to the examples in this collection?
What would help teachers and students connect specialized knowledge with the wider needs of society?
How might the connected subjects of education, scientific discovery, and the preservation of books change your understanding of shared responsibility for learning?

references.label: 1 · Confucius, Analects 2.15 and 2.17 · Study, reflection, and intellectual honesty
references.note: In James Legge’s translation, Confucius cautions against separating learning from thought and describes knowing what one does and does not know as knowledge. Compare this account of disciplined understanding with the compilation’s praise of inquiry and its warnings about pride. These counsels offer a point of conversation between distinct traditions of intellectual and moral formation.

subjects.displayTitle: Knowing oneself: dignity, humility, and discovery
subjects.introduction: Bahá’u’lláh urges His friends to know their own worth, and in the same breath to journey through the horizons and within themselves with penetrating vision. Self-knowledge, in His teaching, begins there: not with a catalogue of tastes or achievements, but with the discernment of what raises a person up and what brings him low. True loss, He warns, belongs to one who spends his days a stranger to himself. The human eye, the Writings observe, sees far into the faults of others and stays blind to its own, and even awareness of the self’s endless intrigues becomes a reason for gratitude, since it keeps the soul awake. Yet the inward road has a horizon it cannot cross: whatever the seeker reaches lies within his own heart, while God remains beyond. The Tao Te Ching likewise prizes mastery of oneself above the conquest of others [1]. From this threshold the way continues into the daily reckoning of one’s own deeds, into the soul as a mirror awaiting light, and into the discipline of teaching oneself before teaching anyone else.
subjects.arc: Begin with worth and practical discernment, examine faults and capacities, explore the limits of spiritual knowledge, and return to service.

order.why: Confront the cost of remaining unknown to oneself.
Open with knowing one’s worth and exploring inwardly and outwardly.
shortened: Say: O friends! Know your own worth and relinquish not your stations.
With perfect wisdom, an illumined heart and penetrating vision, journey through the horizons and within yourselves, and take heed.

order.why: Make self-knowledge a discernment of what elevates or abases.
Turn attention from others’ faults toward one’s own.
shortened: How strange that one should be occupied with the faults of others while heedless of his own faults!

order.why: Expose the asymmetry of that attention.
Keep responsibility for one’s own condition in view.
Connect awareness of shortcomings with growth.
Revisit the protection offered by honest self-examination.
shortened: And has thou realized thy own shortcomings? One must always search for his own shortcomings so that he may repent at the threshold of Oneness and become protected and guarded; otherwise, pride and haughtiness will take possession of one's heart and this will cause deprivation of the bounties of the Court of Singleness.

order.why: Recognize awareness of the self’s intrigues as a beginning.
shortened: The truthful Joseph said: "Verily the soul commands to evil except as my Lord shows mercy." As long as man is aware of this deficiency, he remains awakened and under the shadow of the mercy of the All-Forgiving Lord. But as soon as he shows the slightest negligence, he becomes preserved in vanity and a mine of evil. Therefore give thanks to God that you are aware of the whispers of the self and its endless intrigues.

order.why: Read the reported account of tests revealing strengths and weaknesses.
shortened: Tests are not sent as punishment, but in reality to reveal the soul to itself. Tests reveal strength as well as weakness and provide opportunity to remedy defects.

order.why: Ask whether understanding can be lived.
Introduce inward consultation about action.
shortened: A man may converse with the ego within him saying: "May I do this? Would it be advisable for me to do this work?" Such as this is conversation with the higher self.'

order.why: Locate dignity in knowledge and refinement.
Encourage protection of one’s spiritual station.
shortened: O friends! Know ye your worth and recognize your station, lest what ye have borne in the path of God be lost.

order.why: Picture human worth as a quality yet to become visible.
Name forbearance and godliness as the sword’s true substance.
shortened: Man is like unto a sword, and its essence is forbearance and godliness. So long as it remaineth sheathed in the scabbard of self, its true quality remaineth unknown.

order.why: Retain the parallel source in its own wording.
Turn toward release from self and passion.
Read the call to relinquish imprisoning imaginings.
Hear the invitation to leave the insistent self behind.
Associate selflessness with purity.
Read the shattering of the idol as a spiritual image.
Preserve the criticism of self-centeredness in its educational context.
shortened: They are extremely egotistical and self-centered, yet completely unaware of human virtues and even of the sciences taught in schools.

order.why: Connect reflection to creative and practical knowledge.
shortened: O people of Baha! The source of crafts, sciences and arts is the power of reflection.

order.why: Explore the discovering power of the perceiving soul.
shortened: The "perceiving soul" of man is the power which discovers. Wheresoever it is directed it discovers the hidden mysteries therein, and brings to light that which was veiled.

order.why: Extend inquiry to the mysteries of human reality.
shortened: We must endeavor to discover the world of humanity and the mysteries hidden in the reality of man.

order.why: Consider the reported account of study drawing out latent capacities.
Read the contrast between thought and the material body.
Acknowledge the acquired and limited character of ordinary knowledge.
shortened: Question: What are the limitations imposed upon the powers of the Manifestations of God and, in particular, upon their knowledge?
Answer: Knowledge is of two kinds: existential knowledge and formal knowledge--that is, intuitive knowledge and conceptual knowledge.

The knowledge that people generally have of things consists in conceptualization and observation, that is, either the object is conceived through the rational faculty, or through its observation a form is produced in the mirror of the heart. The scope of this knowledge is quite limited, as it is conditioned upon acquisition and attainment.

order.why: Distinguish intelligible relationships from physical movement.
shortened: For otherwise, egress and regress, descent and inherence are characteristics of bodies and not of spirits--that is, egress and inherence pertain only to sensible realities, not to intelligible subtleties; and intelligible realities, such as reason, love, knowledge, imagination and thought, do not enter, exit or inhere, but rather denote relationships.

For example, knowledge, which is a form acquired by the mind, is an intelligible thing, and to speak of entering into the mind or exiting from it is absurd. Rather, it is a relationship of acquisition, even as images are reflected in a mirror.

order.why: Examine the rational soul through its powers and effects.
shortened: Consider, for instance, the rational soul which is a divine trust deposited within human beings. Observe within thyself how movement and rest, will and purpose, and all else above and below these, as well as hearing, sight, smell, speech, and other outward and inward senses, all exist through its existence. Indeed, were its connection with the body to be severed even slightly, all these senses would be deprived and prevented from their effects and actions.

order.why: Read knowing and reflecting divine glory as a twofold distinction.
Turn inward toward the divine sign.
Connects knowing oneself with knowing God, in a quotation cited by the Bab.
Place this invitation beside the cited Qur’anic signs.
shortened: Even as He hath revealed: "We will surely show them Our signs in the world and within themselves." Again He saith: "And also in your own selves: will ye not then behold the signs of God?" And yet again He revealeth: "And be ye not like those who forget God, and whom He hath therefore caused to forget their own selves." In this connection, He Who is the eternal King -- may the souls of all that dwell within the mystic Tabernacle be a sacrifice unto Him -- hath spoken: "He hath known God who hath known himself."

order.why: Hear the prayer to recognize divine handiwork within.
shortened: I soar not in the kingdoms of the heavens and the earth and all that is between them save that I may know Thy handiwork within myself.

order.why: Read self-knowledge as a purpose of divine teaching.
shortened: "The object of God's teaching to man is that man may know himself in order to comprehend the greatness of God.

order.why: Consider the light by which the self becomes visible.
Give the mirror its needed illumination.
shortened: But the human spirit, unless it be assisted by the spirit of faith, cannot become acquainted with the divine mysteries and the heavenly realities. It is like a mirror which, although clear, bright, and polished, is still in need of light. Not until a sunbeam falls upon it can it discover the divine mysteries.

order.why: Follow that light into understanding sacred writings.
shortened: This light may be likened unto a mirror, and as a mirror reflects all that is before it, so this Light shows to the eyes of our spirits all that exists in God's Kingdom and causes the realities of things to be made visible. By the help of this effulgent Light all the spiritual interpretation of the Holy Writings has been made plain, the hidden things of God's Universe have become manifest, and we have been enabled to comprehend the Divine purposes for man.

order.why: Consider consciousness as a form of vision.
Distinguish the heart’s mysteries from sensory perception.
shortened: The mysteries of love are the secrets of the heart, not something perceived by hearing and sight. They are connected and conditioned upon spiritual sensibilities, not upon worldly senses.

order.why: Read the Four Valleys on the intended meaning of self.
shortened: 9 If the wayfarers be among them that seek after the sanctuary of the Desired One, this plane pertaineth to the self--but the self which is intended is "the Self of God that pervadeth all His laws".
10 This is the plane of the soul that is pleasing unto God, whereof He saith: "Enter thou among My servants, and enter thou My Paradise."

11 This station hath myriad signs and countless tokens. Hence it is said: "We will surely show them Our signs in the world and within themselves, until it become plain to them that there is no God save Him."

order.why: Examine the Bab’s language of signs and the distinction it preserves.
shortened: Look with the eye of thy heart: thy reality is the Lordship of thy Lord for thee through thee - thou art He and He is thou, except that thou art thou and He is He. He has a station of unity, His identity is pure essence - no mention, no indication, no expression of this station except through inability, and this is the perfection of unity through negation of attributes and Lordship, which when there is no object of Lordship has no mention, no encompassing, no manifestation.

order.why: Follow the spiritual path toward recognition.
shortened: The entire Law is but a path for the servant to journey toward his Lord, but through movement toward the pivot We have indicated. As for the way to reach this pivot, know thou that attaining unto the station of thine own reality is attaining unto thy Lord, and it is the station of pure God-fearingness, as one of the Prophets asked about God, saying: "How can one reach Thee?"

order.why: Encounter the limits of what the inward journey can encompass.
shortened: For however much detached minds and pure souls seek to penetrate the worlds of Inner Knowledge, their understanding will never penetrate more than that station which is a sign pointing towards the Monarch of Primal Oneness which He has placed as a trust within the reality of man.  And however much they may fly with triumphant wings in the limitless space of what is knowable and observable, they will read naught but the letters of the book of their own selves.
For example, consider a circle; however much a compass moves, it can only move around the point which is the centre of the circle.

order.why: Retain the reported return of the ascending seeker to the self.
Keep the divine reality beyond the seeker’s reach.
shortened: For were they to reach the ultimate object of their quest for God and their attainment unto Him, they would have but reached that abode which hath been raised up within their own hearts. How then could they ever hope to ascend unto such realms as have not been ordained for them or created for their station? Nay, though they journey from everlasting to everlasting, they will never attain unto Him Who is the midmost Heart of existence and the Axis of the entire creation, He on Whose right hand flow the seas of grandeur, on Whose left stream the rivers of might, and Whose court none can ever hope to reach, how much les His very abode!

order.why: Consider worship as grace that advances the worshipper.
Read the paired affirmations of relationship and creaturely humility.
shortened: When I contemplate, O my God, the relationship that bindeth me to Thee, I am moved to proclaim to all created things "verily I am God!"; and when I consider my own self, lo, I find it coarser than clay!

order.why: Recognize powerlessness within the divine encounter.
shortened: And as for what thou didst mention regarding thy powerlessness and nothingness before His countenance - this indeed is true recognition.

order.why: Hear the surrender of the whole self.
Insist on personal perception rather than inherited acceptance or rejection.
shortened: O Hussein in Sad, He is the Mighty! It hath been known to that honored one that the purpose of creation hath ever been and shall ever be the knowledge of God, and this knowledge dependeth upon the recognition of His servants who perceive the Truth through their own vision and heart and nature, for imitation sufficeth not, whether in acceptance or rejection.

order.why: Connect knowledge with the lessening of fear.
shortened: In the treasuries of the knowledge of God there lieth concealed a knowledge which, when applied, will largely, though not wholly, eliminate fear. This knowledge, however, should be taught from childhood, as it will greatly aid in its elimination. Whatever decreaseth fear increaseth courage.

order.why: Close the linked readings with hearts recreated and souls renewed.
shortened: Methinks that they imagine that Thy purpose in calling them to Thine all-highest horizon is to heighten the glory of Thy majesty and power. For had they been satisfied that Thou summonest them to that which will recreate their hearts and immortalize their souls, they would never have fled from thy governance, nor deserted the shadow of the tree of Thy oneness.
